question: Does parameterized mechanism representation reduce total unique mechanism count and token cost across the existing SPIDER task corpus, providing evidence that deduplication savings could offset per-mechanism token penalty in real agent workflows?
hypothesis: Parameterized mechanisms reduce total registry size and token cost compared to literal (concrete-URL) mechanisms across the task corpus, because multiple tasks sharing the same action pattern (e.g., GET /posts/{id}) collapse to one parameterized mechanism instead of many literal variants.
falsifier: Parameterized representation increases total registry size or token cost compared to literal representation across the task corpus (deduplication ratio > 1.0), OR the deduplication ratio is < 1.0 but the net token cost (parameterized overhead minus deduplication savings) is negative.

baselines.description: All mechanisms stored as literal concrete-URL mechanisms (one per unique URL across all tasks)
baselines.expected_behavior: N_unique_mechanisms equals total distinct concrete URLs; token cost equals sum of all literal mechanism tokens

baselines.description: Mechanisms stored as parameterized templates with slot names (one per unique action pattern across all tasks)
baselines.expected_behavior: N_unique_mechanisms equals distinct action patterns; token cost equals sum of parameterized mechanism tokens including slot syntax

positive_control.description: Tasks sharing the same action pattern (e.g., GET /posts/{id} for different concrete IDs) should collapse to one parameterized mechanism
positive_control.expected_behavior: Parameterized mechanism count for shared patterns equals 1 regardless of number of concrete variants

null_control.description: Tasks with completely distinct action patterns (no sharing) should show no deduplication benefit
null_control.expected_behavior: Deduplication ratio approximately 1.0 when no tasks share action patterns

measurement_validity: Mechanism definitions must come from existing SPIDER registry and task corpus (not synthetic)
Token counting must use tiktoken cl100k_base for consistency with parent experiments
Deduplication ratio must be computed as parameterized_total_tokens / literal_total_tokens
Both GET and non-GET methods must be counted separately to avoid method-conflation bias
decision_rule: SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST requires ALL of: (C1) parameterized mechanism count < literal mechanism count across task corpus; (C2) parameterized total token cost < literal total token cost (deduplication ratio < 1.0); (C3) net token savings (literal_cost - parameterized_cost) > 0; (C4) positive_control passes (shared patterns collapse to 1); (C5) null_control passes (no-sharing patterns show ratio ~1.0). FALSIFIED if any condition fails.
product_consequence_positive: If deduplication ratio < 1.0 with positive net savings, proceed to end-to-end C-PRODUCT-ECON measurement with real agent infrastructure to validate amortized cost benefits in real workflows.
product_consequence_negative: If deduplication ratio >= 1.0 or net savings <= 0, close token-based inheritance viability entirely and pursue alternative product economics (retrieval efficiency, registry size compression, or orthogonal mechanisms).
estimated_cost: Low — purely analytical computation on existing registry/task data, no browser/model/network calls
expected_information_gain: High — directly answers whether deduplication is viable before committing to expensive end-to-end measurement; changes product lane direction if negative
